main_text.l: Dogmata præconis, miracula concomitantur: Illum quæ doceant pectus habere pium.
Quantum sic populum Zabuli de dentibus egit, Et vita & verbo, credere nemo potest.
Lippis lux oculis nocuit: non sustinuere Vivere tam sanctum fœda Romana cohors.
Sistitur hæresis, fidem quod sitiq; sacerdos, Eugenio Papæ, & frivola quæq; patent.
Instituit sacris antistes hunc Rhedonensis, Testis apud Gallos publica fama volat.
Sordida Roma Thomam Papa sordente petebat, Flamma forbendum, quamq; tyrannus alit.
Urget adhoc primas Guilhelmus Rothomagensis, Cardinei cœtus. Sic perit innocuus.
Perstitit igne Thomas, constanti pectore firmus, Quod Christi exemplo vivere clerus habet.
Eugenius memorans tandem, quod infidiosa Morte viri, fuerit credulus ipse malis:
Ingemuit crebro, uir quod tam sanctus obisset, Hoc quoq; præ cunctis conqueritur abiens.
Non nocuit flamma ista Thomæ, sed martyriū dat, Immortalis ei parta corona manet.
Post tormenta pius (sibi dant quæ carcer & ignis) Martyr ad æthereas convolat ille domos.
Præterea, ante Papatum, Eugenius S. Agnetis

page.notes: The stray mark "1" at the left of the first line and the small marks in the left margin are not printed text and are left out. The verse is printed in roman type. The text was copied from a poor scan. Doubtful readings: "sitiq;" and "forbendum" (the latter may be correct as printed). The printed forms "fic", "fustinuere", "fidem" and "poteft" were read as "sic", "sustinuere", "fidem" and "potest" because long s is always a plain s. The printed "obiffet" was read as "obisset". Each distich is one paragraph, since the verse is set in couplets.
